student_card: RN1 — Exactly which numbers are rational?

Classify these exact numbers as rational or irrational and justify: −3;0;2/5;0.125;0.333… with 3 repeating forever;√9;√2;π. State whether each is also an integer. Give a fraction for every rational number and explain why a finite calculator display alone cannot classify an exact number. Diagnostic: evaluate −4+7 and 3/4+1/2. Integers include negative whole numbers, zero and positive whole numbers.
teacher_key: RN1 — Exactly which numbers are rational?

Classify these exact numbers as rational or irrational and justify: −3;0;2/5;0.125;0.333… with 3 repeating forever;√9;√2;π. State whether each is also an integer. Give a fraction for every rational number and explain why a finite calculator display alone cannot classify an exact number. Diagnostic: evaluate −4+7 and 3/4+1/2. Integers include negative whole numbers, zero and positive whole numbers.

Rational:−3=−3/1,0=0/1,2/5,0.125=1/8,0.333…=1/3,√9=3=3/1. Integer members:−3,0,√9. Irrational:√2 andπ. A rational number is expressible as a/b for integers a,b with b≠0. Irrational real numbers cannot be expressed that way. A terminating or eventually repeating decimal is rational. A rounded display is an approximation, not an exact expansion. Diagnostic answers 3 and 5/4. Do not classify every radical as irrational.
